questions.q: What ADLS Gen2 feature makes POSIX-style ACLs possible, on top of Blob Storage?
options: A separate ADLS Gen2 account type unrelated to Blob Storage
Shared access signatures (SAS tokens)
Azure RBAC, which ACLs replace entirely
The hierarchical namespace, which gives the storage account real, traversable folders
questions.explain: ADLS Gen2 is Blob Storage with hierarchical namespace enabled, which is what makes per-folder POSIX-style ACLs possible.

questions.q: A principal has Read and Write set directly on a deeply nested folder, but no Execute on any of its parent folders. What happens?
options: The Read and Write permissions don't work, because every parent directory needs Execute for the principal to traverse into it
Read and Write still work fully, since ACLs ignore parent folders
The portal automatically grants Execute on all parents
Only Write fails; Read still works
questions.explain: The portal's own Manage ACL screen states this directly: Read and Write only work if the principal also has Execute on every parent directory up to the container root.

questions.q: What's the difference between an access ACL and a default ACL on a directory?
options: They are two names for the exact same setting
The default ACL retroactively changes all existing child items
Only blobs can have default ACLs, not directories
The access ACL controls the directory itself; the default ACL is a template applied to new child items created under it going forward
questions.explain: The access ACL governs the object itself. The default ACL — which only appears on directories — sets what new children get when created, without touching existing items.

questions.q: Why does Microsoft recommend assigning ACL entries to Microsoft Entra groups instead of individual users?
options: ACLs technically cannot be assigned to individual user accounts
It removes the need for Azure RBAC entirely
Groups get automatic Execute permission on all parent folders
A group's membership only needs updating once, rather than hunting down every individual ACL entry when someone changes roles
questions.explain: Individual-user ACL entries become a cleanup burden as people change teams; group-based ACLs only need the group membership changed in one place.

questions.q: Can the Azure portal apply an ACL change recursively to every file in a folder tree in one action?
options: Yes, there's a built-in 'Apply recursively' checkbox on every Manage ACL screen
No — the portal only applies ACL changes to one object at a time; recursive changes require Storage Explorer, PowerShell, the CLI, or an SDK
Yes, but only for blobs, never for directories
Only for containers, never for subfolders
questions.explain: The Azure portal is limited to one object at a time for ACL changes; recursive application needs a different tool.
